body:
**Blocked by #167. Contains a security fix — do not defer it.**

### Security: /api/health/cron-status is public

`src/app/api/health/cron-status/route.ts` has **no authentication whatsoever** — no `authorizePermission`, no `getUser`. The only "auth" match in the file is the table name `gmail_oauth_credentials`. It uses `createAdminClient`, the **service-role** client, which bypasses RLS, and returns full cron job status to any anonymous caller. It is absent from ROUTE_PERMISSIONS, so middleware never matches it and skips its auth block entirely.

`getCronStatus()` in `src/actions/system/cron-status.ts` does check `SYSTEM_MONITOR` — but its implementation is a server-side `fetch()` of this same public route, so the check is decorative.

This is a sibling of the `cron/process-report-schedules` hole found earlier.

### Change

1. Add `SYSTEM_MONITOR` authorization to the API route, or route every consumer through the authorized server action and stop `CronHealthCard` fetching it directly from the client.
2. Adopt the richer `/settings/cron-status` UI as canonical at `/system/cron-status`. Retire `/settings/system/health`, which renders only the `CronHealthCard`, and the cron section of the `/settings/system` overview. Three surfaces, two fetch paths, one concern.
3. Fix the `CronHealthCard` "View Detailed Status" link — it currently points at `/settings/system`, which is wrong today regardless of this work.
4. Fix `actionUrl: '/settings/system'` at `src/actions/email/send-admin-alert.ts:158` — a link inside cron-failure alert **emails**, i.e. stale exactly when someone is responding to an outage.

### Docs

`website/docs/integrations/scheduled-jobs.md`, `website/docs/administration/troubleshooting.md`.

### Verify

`npm test`; **unauthenticated curl of `/api/health/cron-status` must be refused.**
